Natural cream, pale blue and soft warm gray, fresh and restful. Clearly morning, not orange sunset. Realistic window scale and aircraft geometry. Primary request: the peaceful first-person feeling of a spacewalk looking down at Earth's night side from low orbit. A gently curved Earth limb crosses the middle of the portrait; deep dark-blue ocean and continental edges far below, with fine warm city-light clusters and a thin restrained teal-green auroral ribbon following part of the atmospheric curve. Sparse faint stars in the upper nearly black indigo space. Vast quiet empty space and Earth's soft curvature are the main subjects. A short small curved piece of a clean pale safety tether enters only along one lower corner, softly lit, enough to suggest the viewer is safely floating without dominating. No astronaut body or glove.
Style: believable orbital long-exposure photography with subtle fine city lights, physically plausible thin aurora rather than giant fantasy curtains. Soft exposure sufficient to see the dark ocean and a little cloud texture, peaceful blue and teal, tiny gold lights. No giant moon, nebula, space station clutter or dramatic storm. Make the night globe gentle and reassuring rather than ominous. No agency markings or technical labels.
